polycrystalline_iron.modulus_source: Takaki et al (2020), polycrystalline Fe E_p=208.2 GPa, DOI:10.2355/tetsutohagane.TETSU-2019-129

polycrystalline_ice.modulus_source: Ewing et al. (1934), approximate dynamic E=9.17 GPa near -5 C, as compiled by McCarthy / Hobbs

limitations: Young's moduli are illustrative literature values obtained under differing temperatures and measurement conditions, not guaranteed values for arbitrary asteroids.
Uniaxial, isotropic, infinitesimal, Hookean, reversible elastic response only; no failure, creep, plasticity, anisotropy, porosity or phase change.
Fixed nominal reference volume and a far-field point-monopole gravitational proxy. Changes of shape, direction, supports and tensor stresses are not solved.
E/c^2 accounts for stored mechanical energy in a chosen sample boundary; loading reduces energy elsewhere in the apparatus. Not an isolated gravitational source creation.
Full general relativity, boundary/support stress-energy and non-spherical multipoles are not calculated. The proxy is not an exact change in the full field of a loaded sample.
No entropy number is computed because dissipative entropy depends on temperature and transport path.
No additional information channel, interaction instruction field or novel gravitational coupling is assumed, derived or experimentally detected.
